docs.title: Faraday Cli
docs.text: Use Faraday directly from your favorite terminal. faraday-cli is the official client that make automating your security workflows, easier.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text: Here you have some snippets of different workflows you can generate using faraday-cli

docs.title: One-line Continuous Scan
docs.text:
Scan assets from workspace.

$ faraday-cli host list -ip -w other_ws | nmap -iL - -oX /tmp/nmap.xml && faraday-cli tool report -w other_ws /tmp/nmap.xml

docs.title: AI pentest with FaradAI
docs.text:
Launch an AI-driven pentest against a target using the FaradAI cloud agent (scanner) and watch it to completion.

$ faraday-cli pentest --target https://example.com --watch
!!! info pentest is the shortcut for faradai scan. Use --advanced for the deeper 80-round audit, or scanners run --agent <id|name> to run any cloud agent with raw parameters. See Commands.

docs.title: One-Line to nmap to all the host in the workspace and import the results back to Faraday
docs.text:
To scan all the host list inside a workspace with nmap and import the results back to faraday.

for ip in $(faraday-cli host list -ip); faraday-cli tool run \"nmap -Pn -p443,80 -sV --script=+http-enum -vvv $ip\"

!!! info In this case it should have a workspace named "other_ws" with hostnames in it

docs.title: Scan your subdomains
docs.text:
Use a tool like assetfinder to do a domains lookup, scan them with nmap and send the results to faraday

$ assetfinder -subs-only example.com| sort | uniq |awk 'BEGIN { ORS = ""; print " {\"target\":\""}
{ printf "%s%s", separator, $1, $2
separator = ","}END { print "\"}" }' | faraday-cli agent run -a 1 -e nmap --stdin
!!! info For this purpouse, an agent is created and already connected to run the nmap executor

docs.title: Send Faraday Executive Reports by mail
docs.text:
Run a daily scan and send your report

$ faraday-cli executive_report create -t \'"generic_default.docx (generic) (Word)"\' --confirmed -d /tmp/report.docx && echo "Faraday Daily Report" | mail -s "Daily Report" user@example.com -A /tmp/report.docx

docs.title: Load your assets from your cloud provider
docs.text:
Here you can list your assets using a cli from your provider (in this example Digital Ocean), then generate a json with that information and use faraday-cli to send it to faraday.

$ doctl compute droplet list --format PublicIPv4,Name --no-header | awk 'BEGIN { ORS = ""; print " ["}
{ printf "%s{\"ip\": \"%s\", \"description\": \"%s\"}", separator, $1, $2
separator = ", "}END { print "] " }' | faraday-cli host create --stdin

Too many secrets?

QW55IGZhbnMgb2YgVGhlIFNuZWFrZXJzPz8gVHJ5IHJ1bm5pbmcgZmFyYWRheS1jbGkgYWZ0ZXIgc2V0dGluZyB0aGlzICJleHBvcnQgS0FLRVJfTU9ERT0xIg

docs.title: Commands
docs.text: All the commands can be run in Shell Mode or Command Mode

docs.title: auth
docs.text:
Authenticate with your faraday server.

$ faraday-cli auth
Faraday url [http://localhost:5985]: http://localhost:5985
User: faraday
Password:
Saving config
✔ Authenticated with faraday: http://localhost:5985
Optional arguments:

Syntax Description -f/--faraday-url FARADAY_URL url of your faraday server -i/--ignore-ssl Ignore SSL certificate validation -u/--user USER Faraday user -p/--password PASSWORD Faraday password -n/--name NAME Session name to save this connection as (default: the server host)

One active connection, multiple saved sessions

faraday-cli keeps one active connection at a time, but remembers the others as named sessions so you can switch instead of being logged in to two servers at once. Logging in with auth (and faradai register/login, which save a faradai-scan session) adds a session and makes it active.

docs.title: auth list
docs.text:
List the saved connection sessions (the active one is marked). Session names default to user@host, so two users on the same server each get their own switchable session instead of overwriting each other.

$ faraday-cli auth list
  ID  ACTIVE    NAME                    KIND    SERVER                            USER             WORKSPACE
----  --------  ----------------------  ------  --------------------------------  ---------------  ----------------
   1  ✔         alice@corp.faradaysec   server  https://corp.faradaysec.com       alice            -
   2            bob@corp.faradaysec     server  https://corp.faradaysec.com       bob              ws_b
   3            faradai-scan            saas    https://scan.apps.faradaysec.com  you@corp.com     ext_corp_com

docs.title: auth use
docs.text:
Switch the active connection to a saved session — by its ID number, its name, or its user/email. Every command (including pentest/triage/scanners) then uses it.

$ faraday-cli auth use 3                 # by ID
$ faraday-cli auth use faradai-scan      # by name
$ faraday-cli auth use you@corp.com      # by user/email (when unique)
Switched to 'faradai-scan' (https://scan.apps.faradaysec.com) — workspace ext_corp_com

docs.title: auth rm
docs.text:
Remove a saved session (by ID, name or user; clears the active connection if it was the active one).

$ faraday-cli auth rm 3
$ faraday-cli auth rm faradai-scan

Faraday token expiration

You may want to change the faraday token expiration time, so you don't have to authenticate so often.

The default is 12 hours.

To do it change de value of api_token_expiration(expressed in seconds) in your faraday server.ini

docs.title: status
docs.text:
Show the status of your current authentication — the connected Faraday server, your user, whether the token is valid, the active workspace, and versions.

$ faraday-cli status
FARADAY SERVER         IGNORE SSL    VERSION    USER     VALID TOKEN    WORKSPACE
---------------------  ------------  ---------  -------  -------------  -----------
http://localhost:5985  False         corp-3.14  faraday  ✔              test

If you also have a FaradAI-scan SaaS session stored, a second table shows it (server, user, token, ext_<domain> workspace):

FaradAI-scan (SaaS):
FARADAI-SCAN SERVER               USER                 VALID TOKEN    WORKSPACE
--------------------------------  -------------------  -------------  ----------------
https://scan.apps.faradaysec.com  you@corp.com         ✔              ext_corp_com

Optional Arguments:

Syntax Description -p/--pretty Show table in a pretty format

docs.title: host create
docs.text:
Create hosts.

Info

You can pass the host data via stdin. 

$ echo '[{"ip": "1.1.1.5", "description": "some text"}]' | faraday-cli host create --stdin

Optional Arguments:

Syntax Description -w WORKSPACE_NAME Workspace name -d/--host-data HOST_DATA Host data in json format --stdin Read host-data from stdin

host data schema: 

{'type': 'array', 'items': {'type': 'object', 'properties':
    {'ip': {'type': 'string'}, 'description': {'type': 'string'},
    'hostnames': {'type': 'array'}}, 'required': ['ip', 'description']}}

Warning

If you pass the host data as an argument it needs to be escaped like this (only in command mode, not in shell mode). 

$ faraday-cli create hosts -d \''[{"ip": "stan.local", "description": "some server"}]'\'

$ faraday-cli vuln update 46 -w test --status closed
Vulnerability updated

Required Arguments:

Syntax Description -id/--vulnerability-id Vulnerability ID

Optional Arguments:

Syntax Description -w WORKSPACE_NAME Workspace name --status STATUS Status of the Vulnerability: open, closed, re-opened, risk-accepted --severity SEVERITY Severity of the Vulnerability: unclassified, info, low, med, high, critical --desc DESCRIPTION Description --name NAME Vulnerability Name --tag TAG Tag to add to the vuln. In case that you want add more than one vuln you can repeat this argument --confirmed CONFIRMED Indicates if the Vulnerability is confirmed: True, False

docs.title: Agents
docs.text:
Info

For these commands you need to have our Faraday Agents configured.

runners alias

Faraday Agents (the local dispatcher runners) are also reachable as runners — runners list, runners get, runners run are synonyms for the agent commands below, kept for the renamed terminology. The server-side scanners live under the separate scanners group.

docs.title: agent list
docs.text:
List all configured agents.

$ faraday-cli agent list
  ID  NAME    ACTIVE    STATUS    EXECUTORS
----  ------  --------  --------  -----------
   2  nico    True      online    nmap

Optional Arguments:

Syntax Description -p/--pretty Show table in a pretty format -j/--json-output Show output in json

docs.title: agent get
docs.text:
Get information of and agent and its executors.

$ faraday-cli agent get 2
   ID  NAME    ACTIVE    STATUS
----  ------  --------  --------
   2  nico    True      online

Executors:
  ID  NAME    PARAMETERS [REQUIRED]
----  ------  -----------------------
   2  nmap    target [True]
              option_pn [False]
              option_sc [False]
              option_sv [False]
              port_list [False]
              top_ports [False]
              host_timeout [False]
              script_timeout [False]

Required Arguments:

Syntax Description AGENT_ID ID of the Agent

Optional Arguments:

Syntax Description -p/--pretty Show table in a pretty format -j/--json-output Show output in json

docs.title: agent run
docs.text:
Run an executor.

Info

You can pass the executor parameters via stdin. 

$ echo '{"target": "www.google.com"}' | faraday-cli agent run -a 1 -e nmap --stdin --workspace-name my_workspace
If no -p or --stdin argument is provided, then the executor parameters will be asked one by one.

You can store the parameters in env variables and will be auto loaded.

Example: 

For the TARGET parameter of the NMAP executor save the variable FARADAY_CLI_EXECUTOR_NMAP_TARGET

You can store the parameters in a file and use it as a 'profile' to repeat scans 

$ cat scan_test.com_nmap.vars
FARADAY_CLI_EXECUTOR_NMAP_TARGET=test.com
FARADAY_CLI_EXECUTOR_NMAP_OPTION_PN=true
FARADAY_CLI_EXECUTOR_NMAP_OPTION_SC=false
FARADAY_CLI_EXECUTOR_NMAP_OPTION_SV=true
FARADAY_CLI_EXECUTOR_NMAP_PORT_LIST=
FARADAY_CLI_EXECUTOR_NMAP_TOP_PORTS=
FARADAY_CLI_EXECUTOR_NMAP_HOST_TIMEOUT=
FARADAY_CLI_EXECUTOR_NMAP_SCRIPT_TIMEOUT=

$ source scan_test.com_nmap.vars && faraday-cli agent run -a 2 -e nmap -w test
Running executor: unnamed_agent/nmap
Parameters: {"TARGET": "test.com", "OPTION_PN": "true", "OPTION_SC": "false", "OPTION_SV": "true"}
Generated Command: 14

Warning

If you pass the executor parameters as an argument it needs to be escaped like this (only in command mode, not in shell mode). 

$ faraday-cli  agent run -a 1 -e nmap -p \''{"target": "www.go ogle.com"}'\'
Running executor: unnamed_agent/nmap
Parameters: {"TARGET": "www.google.com"}
Generated Command: 13

Required Arguments:

Syntax Description -a/--agent-id AGENT_ID ID of the agent -e/--executor-name EXECUTOR_NAME Executor name -p/--executor-params EXECUTOR_PARAMS Executor Params in json -w --workpsace-name Workspace name

Optional Arguments:

Syntax Description --stdin Read executor-params from stdin

docs.title: Scanners (cloud agents)
docs.text:
Info

Scanners are Faraday cloud agents (the v3/cloud_agents API) — the server-side security agents, distinct from the local Faraday Agents / runners above. This is the generic group: list any cloud agent and run it with arbitrary parameters. FaradAI is one such scanner, so it can be launched here (scanners run --agent faradai ...) or via its own richer faradai command.

docs.title: scanners list
docs.text:
List the cloud agents (scanners) available on the server.

$ faraday-cli scanners list
  ID  NAME            SLUG             CATEGORY   LAST_RUN
----  --------------  ---------------  ---------  ----------
   2  FaradAI         faradai          pentest    ...
   4  FaradAI Triage  faradai-triage   triage     ...
Parameter Description -j, --json-output Show output in json -p, --pretty Show table in a pretty format

docs.title: scanners get
docs.text:
Show a single cloud agent and the parameters it accepts (useful before scanners run so you know which --param keys to pass).

$ faraday-cli scanners get 2
Parameter Description scanner_id ID of the cloud agent (required) -j, --json-output Show output in json -p, --pretty Show table in a pretty format

docs.title: scanners run
docs.text:
Launch any cloud agent against one or more workspaces with arbitrary parameters. The agent is selected by id or by a name/slug fragment.

$ faraday-cli scanners run --agent faradai -w my_workspace \
    --param TARGET=https://example.com --param ROUNDS=20 --watch

# equivalent, params as a JSON object
$ faraday-cli scanners run -a 2 -w my_workspace \
    --params-json '{"TARGET": "https://example.com", "MODE": "Dual", "ROUNDS": 20}'
Parameter Description -a, --agent Cloud-agent id or name/slug fragment (required) -w, --workspace Workspace name (repeatable); defaults to the active one --param KEY=VALUE Run parameter (repeatable). Bare integers and true/false are coerced. --params-json All run params as one JSON object (alternative to repeated --param) --watch Poll the launched command(s) until they finish

--watch

After launching, --watch polls the workspace's command list every ~15s and prints each command as it finishes, then Run finished.. Press Ctrl-C to stop watching — the run keeps going server-side. (The scan itself runs on the server; --watch only follows it.)

Only executor inputs go in --param

A cloud agent has two kinds of fields: its executor run inputs (e.g. First Scan's target) and its stored configuration (resolve_hostname, ignore_info, tags, default workspaces…). Only run inputs may be passed with --param — configuration is set on the agent itself in the Faraday web UI. The CLI validates your --param keys against the agent's input schema before launching and lists the accepted keys on a mismatch (scanners get <id> shows them too). Workspace always goes via -w, never as a param.

docs.title: FaradAI
docs.text:
Info

FaradAI is a Faraday cloud agent (a scanner), with its own command for the common cases: tiered scans, triage, and the FaradAI-scan SaaS onboarding. To list cloud agents use scanners list; to run FaradAI with raw parameters use scanners run --agent faradai.

Shortcuts

The two common actions have top-level shortcuts: faraday-cli pentest (= faradai scan) and faraday-cli triage (= faradai triage). All the flags below apply to the shortcut too.

Backend is auto-selected

faradai scan / faradai triage run against your connected Faraday server when you're authenticated (faraday-cli auth), and against the FaradAI-scan SaaS when you're not. You only need --standalone to force the SaaS path when a server is also connected. A first-time SaaS user with no account is walked through register + verify inline.

Register with an email on the domain you're scanning

A self-registered SaaS account is scoped to ext_<your-email-domain> and can only scan that domain and its subdomains. Registering you@gmail.com (or any public provider, or another company's domain) to scan faradaysec.com will be rejected — public providers get no scan scope at all. During inline onboarding the CLI checks your email against the --target before sending the code and warns if they don't match. Use an email at the target's domain, or have an operator authorize your account.

docs.title: faradai scan
docs.text:
Launch a FaradAI pentest against a target. The FaradAI cloud agent is auto-discovered by name/slug; pass --agent-id to select it explicitly.

# shortcut — against the connected server, or the SaaS when not authenticated
$ faraday-cli pentest --target https://example.com

# full form
$ faraday-cli faradai scan --target https://example.com --workspace my_workspace

$ faraday-cli faradai scan --target https://example.com -w my_workspace --advanced --watch
Parameter Description --target URL/host to scan (required) -w, --workspace Workspace name (repeatable); defaults to the active one --instruction Pentest instruction (default: the FaradAI wizard's staged template for the tier — standard or advanced) --goal Free-text goal/focus for the run (wizard GOAL; empty by default) --mode Dual (default), Claude, or Codex --rounds Max agent rounds (default: 20 standard; 80 with --advanced). Explicit --rounds overrides the tier. --advanced Advanced (deeper) scan — 80 rounds + the wizard full-audit instruction, instead of the standard 20 --agent-id Explicit cloud-agent id (skips FaradAI auto-discovery) --watch Poll the launched command(s) until they finish --standalone Force the FaradAI-scan SaaS backend (auto-used when no server is connected)

Instructions match the web wizard

faradai scan (standard/advanced) and faradai triage launch with the same staged instruction templates the FaradAI web wizard sends — standard → standard, --advanced → full-audit, triage → triage. Override with --instruction for a custom run.

docs.title: faradai triage
docs.text:
Run a FaradAI triage over the existing findings of one or more workspaces (re-test/reproduce, enrich, optionally auto-close false positives). This targets the separate FaradAI Triage cloud agent (auto-discovered); triage has no --target — it works over --workspace findings, not a URL.

# shortcut
$ faraday-cli triage --workspace my_workspace --severities critical,high --reproduce

# full form
$ faraday-cli faradai triage --workspace my_workspace --severities critical,high --reproduce
Parameter Description -w, --workspace Workspace to triage (repeatable, at least one required) --severities Comma-separated severities (e.g. critical,high,medium) --confirmed-only Only triage findings already marked confirmed --auto-close-fp Auto-close findings determined to be false positives --target-filter Only triage findings matching this target/host filter --reproduce Actively re-test (reproduce) each finding --batch-size Findings per triage batch --rounds Max agent rounds --goal Free-text goal for the triage run --instruction Triage instruction (default: the wizard's staged triage template) --agent-id Explicit cloud-agent id (skips auto-discovery) --watch Poll the launched command(s) until they finish --standalone Force the FaradAI-scan SaaS backend (auto-used when no server is connected) --dry-run Plan without mutating findings

docs.title: FaradAI-scan SaaS (register / verify / login)
docs.text:
Info

The FaradAI-scan SaaS (https://faradai-scan.apps.faradaysec.com) lets you self-register from the CLI — no Faraday web UI. New accounts get one free scan per tier; further scans need purchased credits.

Zero-to-scan flow:

$ faraday-cli faradai register --email you@corp.com
# → a strong password is generated and shown; a 6-digit code is emailed
$ faraday-cli faradai verify 123456
$ faraday-cli faradai scan --target https://example.com --standalone

Or skip straight to scanning — a first-time --standalone scan with no account yet walks you through register + verify inline, then runs:

$ faraday-cli faradai scan --target https://example.com --standalone
No FaradAI-scan account yet — let's create one.
Email: you@corp.com
# → password generated + shown, code emailed
Verification code (check your email): 123456
Launching FaradAI scan ...

register stashes the email + password, so verify needs only the code. Pass --password to choose your own; omit it and one is generated for you and printed once (save it — it's what you log in with later). Returning users re-authenticate without a new code:

$ faraday-cli faradai login --email you@corp.com

The credentials are stored under the faradai_scan section of ~/.faraday-cli.yml, separate from your main auth server connection. The pending email/password are cleared from the config once verify succeeds (the token is what persists).

verify and login also store your ext_<domain> workspace (when your account is scoped to a single one), so later scans need only --target.

Workspace auto-discovery

You rarely need --workspace for a scan. When you have access to exactly one workspace (the usual case for a scan user), faradai scan resolves it automatically — on both the authenticated (auth) and --standalone paths. Pass --workspace only when you can access several. faradai triage always requires --workspace (the workspace IS the triage target).

Command Parameters faradai register --email (required), --password, --dashboard-url faradai verify --email (required), --code (required), --password, --dashboard-url faradai login --email (required), --password, --scan-url

docs.title: Executive Reports
docs.text:
Info

These commands only work with a commercial version of Faraday.

docs.title: executive_report list-templates
docs.text:
List the templates available to generate Executive Reports.

$ faraday-cli executive_report list-templates -p
+------------------------------------------------------------------+-----------+
| NAME                                                             | GROUPED   |
|------------------------------------------------------------------+-----------|
| generic_default.docx (generic) (Word)                            | False     |
| generic_default.html (generic) (PDF)                             | False     |
| group_default.docx (grouped) (Word)                              | True      |
| group_default.html (grouped) (PDF)                               | True      |
+------------------------------------------------------------------+-----------+

Optional Arguments:

Syntax Description -w WORKSPACE_NAME Workspace name -p/--pretty Show table in a pretty format

docs.title: executive_report create
docs.text:
Generate an executive report with a given template.

$ faraday-cli executive_report create -t \'"generic_default.html (generic) (PDF)"\'  --title title --summary summary --enterprise company  -d /tmp/test.pdf  --ignore-info
Report created: /tmp/test.pdf

Optional Arguments:

Syntax Description -w WORKSPACE_NAME Workspace name -t/--template TEMPLATE Template --title TITLE Report title --summary SUMMARY Report summary --recommendations RECOMMENDATIONS Report recommendations --conclusions CONCLUSIONS Report conclusions --scope SCOPE Report scope --objectives OBJECTIVES Report objectives --enterprise ENTERPRISE Enterprise name --confirmed Confirmed vulnerabilities --severity [SEVERITY [SEVERITY ...]] Filter by severity informational/critical/high/medium/low/unclassified --ignore-info Ignore informational/unclassified vulnerabilities -d/--destination DESTINATION Report destination

docs.title: help
docs.text:
Using the help command you can get info of any command. 

$ faraday-cli help -v

Documented commands (use 'help -v' for verbose/'help <topic>' for details):

Core
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
auth                Authenticate with a faraday server
exit                exit the application. Shorthand: Ctrl-D.
status              Show Cli status
version             Faraday cli version

Objects
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
agent               agent actions
executive_report    executive_report actions
host                host actions
service             service actions
tool                tool actions
vuln                vulnerabilities actions
workspace           workspace actions
...


$  faraday-cli help auth
usage: auth [-h] [-f FARADAY_URL] [-i] [-u USER] [-p PASSWORD]

Authenticate with a faraday server

optional arguments:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -f FARADAY_URL, --faraday-url FARADAY_URL
                        Faraday server URL
  -i, --ignore-ssl      Ignore SSL verification
  -u USER, --user USER  Faraday user
  -p PASSWORD, --password PASSWORD
                        Faraday password

docs.title: Installation Instructions
docs.text:
Before installing, we recommend creating and activating a Python virtual environment to avoid affecting your system Python packages. For example:

python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate

You can also use virtualenv if you prefer. Once the virtual environment is active, run the installation commands below.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
pip 
$ pip install faraday-cli
git 
$ git clone https://github.com/infobyte/faraday-cli.git
$ cd faraday-cli
$ pip install .

Python version

Python 3.7 and up required.

docs.title: Create a workspace or select active Workspace
Process reports from any of the many tools we support
Or run the tools with faraday-cli
docs.text:
Faraday Cli can be used in two modes:

  • shell mode: faraday-cli reacts as a shell to your commands
  • command mode: faraday-cli reacts as a command with parameters

docs.title: Shell Mode
docs.text:
In this mode Faraday-cli will react as a shell, so if you type an OS command it will process it as a shell.

If auto_command_detection is enabled it will try to process any tool we support to send the info to faraday.

docs.title: Change settings
docs.text:
You can change some settings from the cli itself.

  • custom_plugins_path (Path where the cli will look for custom plugins)
  • ignore_info_severity (If set to True the cli will ignore all INFORMATIONAL vulnerabilities) [DEFAULT: False]
  • auto_command_detection (If set to True the cli will try process a tool when is run in shell mode) [DEFAULT: True]
$ faraday-cli

docs.title: Global Configurations
docs.text:
You can list or change some settings from the cli itself.

$ faraday-cli set
+------------------------+----------+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|          Name          |  Value   |                                   Description                                    |
+------------------------+----------+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| allow_style            | Terminal | Allow ANSI text style sequences in output (valid values:Always, Never, Terminal) |
| always_show_hint       | False    | Display tab completion hint even when completion suggestions print               |
| auto_command_detection | True     | Enable/disable automatic command detection                                       |
| custom_plugins_path    | None     | Path of custom plugins folder                                                    |
| echo                   | False    | Echo command issued into output                                                  |
| editor                 | vim      | Program used by 'edit'                                                           |
| feedback_to_output     | False    | Include nonessentials in '|', '>' results                                        |
| hostname_resolution    | True     | Enable/disable hostname resolution                                               |
| ignore_info_severity   | False    | Ignore Informational vulnerabilities from reports and commands                   |
| max_completion_items   | 50       | Maximum number of CompletionItems to display during tab completion               |
| quiet                  | False    | Don't print nonessential feedback                                                |
| timing                 | False    | Report execution times                                                           |
+------------------------+----------+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

$ faraday-cli set hostname_resolution False
hostname_resolution - was: True
now: False
